thread:
Sasha: Quick sync - proposing a compact routing policy + console surface for headroom-triggered routing and model-variant fallbacks by customer tier/region. Posting an example and asking for telemetry + CB threshold feedback.

Liam: two quick clarifying questions: which latency percentile should the policy use for gating (p95 vs p99)? And how do we define availability (5xx only or include timeouts/client cancels)? Those choices change circuit-breaker sensitivity.

Priya: suggest p95 for most tiers, p99 optional for platinum/enterprise. Define availability as 5xx + backend timeouts (server-side). Use a rolling 5m window for metrics.

Carlos: note on region residency: private/VPC customers should be opt-out for cross-region fallback. Policy needs allowlist of fallback regions and a flag to forbid cross-region fallback.

Emmie: console UX: add route-level SLO pills (green/amber/red) and an expand panel showing current windowed stats and recent fallback events. Include an "override" action with RBAC + audit trail for enterprise. Rollout wizard should prefill safe CB defaults.

Sasha: compact policy example (as text) to illustrate intent - this is not the API yet:

```
{
  "tier": "enterprise",
  "slo_latency_p95_ms": "120",
  "slo_availability_pct": "99.9",
  "cb_window_s": "300",
  "cb_error_rate_pct": "0.1",
  "cb_min_requests": "100",
  "fallback_order": "gptx-8b,gptx-4b",
  "fallback_max_qps": "50",
  "allow_fallback_regions": "us-west-2,eu-central-1",
  "cross_region_fallback_allowed": "false"
}
```

Sasha: semantics: when the p95 or availability breaches for the window and min_requests are met, trigger CB and route to next variant in fallback_order, but respect region allowlist and cross-region flag.

Liam: implementation notes: 1) after a CB trip, use exponential backoff for recheck intervals to avoid oscillation; 2) evaluate both absolute latency vs target and relative delta vs baseline traffic to avoid false positives during sudden load changes.

Priya: also track fallback_count per customer+variant and emit weekly deltas. Alert if fallback_count rises > 30% week-over-week or if fallbacks cause quality regressions.

Carlos: infra concerns: smaller fallback models change KV cache behavior and tokenization cost. Add telemetry tags for model_variant and kv_cache_hit to attribute latency/cost correctly. Also ensure fallback skip logic if target model reports saturation.

deploy-bot: [deploy] canary routing-policy-service v2 started in us-west-2: https://ci/repo/1234

Emmie: question - should console allow per-customer override or only org-level? For enterprise customers we need per-customer overrides with RBAC and expiry.

Sasha: plan: per-customer overrides allowed for enterprise, audited and time-limited. Rollout wizard will surface that option.

Liam: telemetry events to emit: route, model_variant, region, customer_tier, latency_ms, status_code, queue_ms, backend_util_pct, cb_event (reason, window_s, metric_snapshot, fallback_target).

Priya: quotas interaction: when falling back to cheaper model, billing and quota accounting must map consumed tokens to the fallback model so invoicing remains correct. Fallback should also check quota headroom to avoid cascading failures when fallback model has no quota.

Carlos: policy should include a behavior when fallback targets are saturated: skip to next eligible target or return structured 503 with machine-readable reason so clients can degrade gracefully.

Sasha: owners & next steps: PR for API schema and enforcement semantics (owner: @Sasha) - target Fri; console mocks for SLO pills, override UX, rollout wizard (owner: @Emmie) - next Wed; telemetry/event schema (owner: @Liam) - start EOD; simulation runs (burst/gradual/regional outage) on policy-sim (owner: @Carlos/@Priya).

Sasha: anything blocking before I open the PR?

Liam: no infra blockers, I'll add backoff heuristics in PR comments.

Priya: will draft alerts for fallback_count and SLO burn.

Carlos: will add region-residency tests to sim and ensure private customers default to no cross-region fallback.

Emmie: will drop Figma mocks here when ready.

Sasha: great, thanks everyone :thumbsup:
